newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinea hit by landslide, 43 killed.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea hit by landslide, 43 killed.

text.p: Officials in the South Pacific nation of Papua New Guinea said on Tuesday that 43 people had died in a landslide overnight.
The nation's Director of Disaster and Emergency Services Leith Anderson said a whole village near Menyamya was buried and 43 people, including a number of children, had been trapped.
"It looks very bad," Anderson said of the landslide at Menyamya, inland from Lae on the north coast of the Papua New Guinea mainland.
He said the landslide was the result of heavy rains in the area over the past few days.
Landslides are common in the mountains around the small township of Menyamya which are are so steep and fragmented that Australian explorers in the 1930s called the area "broken bottle country".
A detailed statement was expected later on Tuesday from Provincial Affairs Minister Peter Barter, who visited the area this morning.
Anderson earlier issued strong wind and heavy rain warnings for all parts of the country, warning people not to venture out into the open unnecessarily and to look out for falling trees.
The capital, Port Moresby, and other parts of Papua New Guinea have seen strong winds and heavy rains in recent days.
